findings.reason: the node's first task would be disproving its own deliverable, and the fix scope changes from "route it through the existing channel" to "design a channel a live round can read mid-turn".
findings.text: §31 asks a running repair round to take a widen "before its next tool call, through the same channel a widen reaches a working run", but at main there is no such channel: `widen_claim` refuses a live run's amendment with "its worker is still running; wait for that process to exit" (reckon/crew/claims.py:113-116), and `widen_takes_effect` states the model the fix would have to overturn — "A running worker's mounts are fixed when its sandbox starts, so a widened claim reaches it only on its next attempt" (reckon/crew/claims.py:157-158). The Why also describes the incident as a widen that "added the file", where the refusal above means it most likely did not; the node would arrive expecting to reuse an existing delivery route and find it has to build one — an investigation whose premise the code contradicts.

findings.reason: the case as written measures the pointer rather than the round's reachable fence, and would go green on a repair that fixes nothing.
findings.text: §31's first done-when case is "a widen issued during an automatic repair round appears in the round's write paths", a read of the pointer; the pointer's write paths can be written while the running worker's mount set is unchanged (claims.py:157-158), so the assertion passes on a change that leaves the worker still unable to write the file it needs — which is the entire defect. The declared negative control restores the advice refusal and reddens only the advice case, so no control shows this case can fail.

findings.reason: the node's own gate would skip the population covering half its write paths.
findings.text: §31's regression gate names "the test files importing `reckon.crew.recovery_repair_dispatch`" while its write paths also include the module that issues the resume refusal (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2345`); no test that imports that module is in the measured population, so a regression introduced in the advice half — the half the incident was reported for — would not be seen. §32 states the correct form ("the test files importing the changed modules").

findings.reason: either the goal narrows to the duplicate and the resume variant becomes its own section, or the done-when must demand a reproduction for the resume path too; as written the node can close with the second defect unexplained.
findings.text: §30 is titled for the duplicate review of one head, but its deliverable carries two separately caused defects: the 39-second duplicate (a manual dispatch followed by the reflex's) and the pre-resume head dispatched after a widen-and-resume, which the Why already calls "a head about to move". The done-when reproduces only one sequence ("two review pointers for one head") and its proposed sections must cover both, so one verdict cannot close it and the second variant's evidence is never required.

findings.reason: an ambiguous fence stalls the node once it starts writing, and the two candidate modules are in different files.
findings.text: §32's write paths read "the review-record checker and the review repair command modules, and the new test", naming no file, while the checker it means is `review_record_refusals` in `reckon/crew/review.py:932` and the repair command in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1229`; every other section in the plan names its files. A dispatched worker's fence is built from literal paths, so this description must be resolved by guesswork or a scope extension before the first edit.

findings.reason: its cases are red at main by construction, so the node would discover the state at once and the missing clause costs a sentence rather than a wrong path.
findings.text: _document states "Each section opens by confirming that its defect still reproduces at main" (plan.html:34-35), and §31 and §30 both carry a reproduction step, but §32's deliverable opens straight at "Three changes" with no reproduce-at-main clause — although its first, second and fourth cases would fail at main today (`review_record_refusals` compares no id at reckon/crew/review.py:932-972, and `--set` accepts only status/subject at :3523-3524), so the confirmation is cheap and the omission is the document's own claim going unmet.
